previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, multiple abdominal surgeries, and chronic leukocytosis was admitted for abdominal pain and nausea consistent with a gastroparesis flare. Imaging showed no obstruction or acute abdominal process, and infectious workup was negative. She was managed with NPO status, GJ tube feeds, and symptom control using morphine and lorazepam. Her leukocytosis persisted but was deemed chronic and non-infectious. Hypertension was addressed with initiation of lisinopril, titrated to 40 mg daily. TSH was mildly elevated at 6.0, likely due to malabsorption or illness, with plans to recheck as an outpatient. She improved clinically, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in GI and primary care.

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a very pleasant
___ female who was previously seen in Breast Surgery
Clinic on ___, to discuss the new diagnosis of left
breast recurrent carcinoma.

Her past medical and past surgical history is significant for
left breast cancer diagnosed in ___ and treated at ___. 
Per outside records, she had an infiltrating carcinoma of the
left breast with a lumpectomy followed by a reexcision and an
axillary lymph node dissection of 17 nodes showing all of them
negative for carcinoma.  Thereafter, she underwent adjuvant
radiation therapy at ___.  No endocrine or
chemotherapy was given thereafter.

More recently, calcifications in the right breast were being
watched on mammogram in the retroareolar region.  In ___,
her mammogram showed a new asymmetry in the superior posterior
aspect of the left breast for which additional imaging was
recommended.  She had an ill-defined hypoechoic shadowing
measuring 1 cm in size at the 11 to 12 o'clock position in the
left breast.  She underwent image-guided core biopsy of the left
breast lesion on ___, resulting as invasive lobular
carcinoma, grade 2 with receptors pending.  She was thus
diagnosed with recurrent left breast carcinoma and presented to
our Breast Surgery Clinic at that time to discuss the clinical
and surgical treatment plan.

We discussed options for management.  At the time of her visit
with us, we did not receive her outside imaging and thus cannot
have it reviewed at our institution.  Subsequently, it has
arrived.  Subsequently, the imaging was received and it was
reviewed by Dr. ___ in Radiology.  Other diagnostic 
mammogram
in ___ of the small coarse heterogeneous calcifications in
the lower outer subareolar right breast were noted, which were
not significantly changed in comparison to prior studies.  There
was, however, new spiculated mass in the upper inner left breast
at middle depth for which further imaging was recommended. 
Ultrasound was reviewed at the region of the 11 to 12 o'clock
position, 5 cm from the nipple, there was a 1.1 x 1.0 x 0.7 cm
hypoechoic mass with indistinct margins corresponding to the
mammographic mass.  This was subsequently biopsied and clip was
placed within the mass.  A single image of the left axilla was
reviewed that did not show any abnormal-appearing lymph nodes. 
An MRI was recommended to further assess the bilateral breasts
due to the aforementioned findings.

She did have an MRI on ___.  A round mass with
irregular margins and heterogeneous enhancement was noted in the
upper inner quadrant of the left breast measuring 1.3 x 1.2 x 
1.1
cm in size corresponding to the biopsy-proven carcinoma.  No
adenopathy was noted.  No other abnormalities were identified. 
No MRI evidence of malignancy within the right breast.

Her pathology as well was not available at the time of our
initial consultation in clinic.  More recently, this has become
available and the biopsy on ___, was reviewed by Dr.
___ in our ___ Department.  The left breast lesion at
the 11 to 12 o'clock position, 5 cm from the nipple, there is an
invasive carcinoma with predominant lobular features noted, 
grade
2 with ER positive, PR positive and HER-2/neu negative per
report.

Ms. ___ did meet with Dr. ___ in Plastic ___ to discuss
reconstructive options on ___, as we discussed
mastectomy, the standard of care in this clinical situation. 
However, she has decided not to proceed with reconstruction at
this time.

We did discuss her case at the tumor board conference on ___.  The multidisciplinary group recommendations were to omit 
a
sentinel lymph node biopsy given that an axillary lymph node
dissection previously done on ___, revealing 17 lymph
nodes and also thereafter, she had received radiation therapy. 
Given her age and the previous axillary lymph node dissection 
and
radiation treatment to the axilla, it was thought that sentinel
lymph node biopsy would not be necessary for the adjuvant 
therapy
decision making.

I am in favor of omitting the sentinel lymph node biopsy as 
well.

We did discuss her upcoming surgical plan with Dr. ___ vascular surgeon who is following her for chronic SMA
dissection.  Dr. ___ her with an annual
ultrasound.  He reports there are no concerns or issues from his
standpoint for us to proceed with a planned mastectomy for the
recurrent left breast cancer.  He does recommend control of her
blood pressure and that will be achieved by anesthesia
colleagues.

Ms. ___ unfortunately does report she had a recent accident
in swimming pool.  She was trying to get out of the pool and the
water was not available and as she was being lifted up she
unfortunately hit her chest and abdomen against the side of the
pool.  She reports that she had significant chest discomfort and
was evaluated at ___.  Per her report, there
were no acute issues from the injury; however, she started to
have soreness over the chest wall particularly on the right 
side.
 Though the issue of concern is that her GJ tube appears not to
be quite top against her skin as it was before and there was 
some
discomfort at the site.  She is going to be seeing her physician
in ___ later today to ask if she would need
any further evaluation of the GJ tube.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the breast surgery service for 
overnight observation after undergoing a total left mastectomy 
for recurrent left breast cancer (grade 2 invasive lobular 
carcinoma, ER/PR+) previously treated with lumpectomy and 
radiation therapy. The procedure was uncomplicated (see 
Operative Report for further details) and a single drain was 
left in place in the left chest to bulb suction. The patient did 
well post-operatively in the PACU and was transferred to the 
floor in stable condition. She voided appropriately, tolerated 
first clears then a regular diet, and had her pain well 
controlled on oral agents. Use of narcotic analgesia was 
minimized in order to prevent exacerbation of her severe 
gastroperesis. Instead, she received Tylenol and tramadol, as 
needed, with good relief. She ambulated, wore SCDs, and used the 
incentive spirometer effectively. She was afebrile and 
hemodynamically stable throughout her hospital course. She was 
discharged home on POD1 in good condition with visiting nurse 
services set up for drain care. She will be seen for follow up 
in breast surgery clinic in one week.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the breast surgery service after undergoing 
a left total mastectomy (removal of all your left breast 
tissue). Your procedure went well and you did well 
post-operatively. You are being discharged home in stable 
condition with visiting nursing services for your drain. 

Please follow the directions below;

Personal Care: 
1. You may remove your surgical dressing after 48 hours and 
leave your incision open to air.
2. Clean around the drain site(s), where the tubing exits the 
skin, with soap and water. 
3. Strip drain tubing, empty bulb(s), and record output(s) ___ 
times per day. 
4. A written record of the daily output from your drain should 
be brought to every follow-up appointment. Your drain will be 
removed as soon as possible when the daily output tapers off to 
an acceptable amount. 
5. You may shower daily. No baths until instructed to do so by 
Dr. ___.
6. You may wear a soft, non-restrictive camisole but no tight or 
underwire bras. 

Activity: 
1. You may resume your regular diet. 
2. DO NOT lift anything heavier than 5 pounds or engage in 
strenuous activity for two weeks. 

Medications: 
1. Resume your regular medications unless instructed otherwise 
and take any new meds as ordered. 
2. You may take your prescribed pain medication for moderate to 
severe pain. You may switch to Tylenol or Extra Strength Tylenol 
for mild pain as directed on the packaging. Please note that 
Percocet and Vicodin have Tylenol as an active ingredient so do 
not take these meds with additional Tylenol. 
3. Take prescription pain medications (tramadol) for pain not 
relieved by tylenol.
4.Take Colace, 100 mg by mouth 2 times per day, while taking the 
prescription pain medication. You may use a different 
over-the-counter stool softener if you wish. 
5. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while taking any 
narcotic pain medication. You may have constipation when taking 
narcotic pain medications (tramadol, oxycodone, percocet, 
vicodin, hydrocodone, dilaudid, etc.); you should continue 
drinking fluids, you may take stool softeners, and should eat 
foods that are high in fiber. 

Call the office IMMEDIATELY if you have any of the following: 
1. Signs of infection: fever with chills, increased redness, 
swelling, warmth or tenderness at the surgical site, or unusual 
drainage from the incision(s). 
2. A large amount of bleeding from the incision(s) or drain(s). 
3. Fever greater than 101.5 oF 
4. Severe pain NOT relieved by your medication. 

Return to the ER if: 
* If you are vomiting and cannot keep in fluids or your 
medications. 
* If you have shaking chills, fever greater than 101.5 (F) 
degrees or 38 (C) degrees, increased redness, swelling or 
discharge from incision, chest pain, shortness of breath, or 
anything else that is troubling you. 
* Any serious change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that 
concern you. 

DRAIN DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS 
You are being discharged with drains in place. Drain care is a 
clean procedure. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and warm 
water before performing drain care. Perform drainage care twice 
a day. Try to empty the drain at the same time each day. Pull 
the stopper out of the drainage bottle and empty the drainage 
fluid into the measuring cup. Record the amount of drainage 
fluid on the record sheet. Reestablish drain suction.
Thank you for allowing us to participate in your care.
